proposals.entity_key: Main clause verbs followed by que
value: Limited to main clause reporting verbs such as dire, affirmer, annoncer, savoir
The dependent clause is usually in the indicative, not the subjunctive
Que is replaced by si when the dependent clause is an indirect yes/no question

evidence.notes: First two entries come from the rule text; the si substitution follows from the listed expressions (savoir si).

value: Applies only to qualificative adjectives, not to determiners or numbers
Short common adjectives (e.g. grand, petit, beau, jeune, bon) precede the noun instead
Adjectives followed by a complement always come after the noun

evidence.notes: Derived from the stated default placement and its exception; the complement restriction is standard usage with medium confidence.

value: Limited to un, une, des and the partitive articles after a negated verb
Not applied after être, which keeps un/une (Il n'est pas un expert)

evidence.notes: Second entry reflects the standard exception to de-negation and is flagged as a possible addition beyond the source text.

value: ne and pas surround only the auxiliary, never the past participle
Requires a compound tense with an auxiliary; a simple conjugated verb is negated differently

evidence.notes: Directly from the rule's word order and the stated trap.

value: Applies only to a non-conjugated infinitive
ne and pas remain together before the infinitive and are never split around it

evidence.notes: Both entries restate the rule's formation and trap.

value: Requires at least two negated nouns; a single noun uses pas de
Definite articles (le, la, l', les) are kept, while indefinite and partitive articles disappear
ne precedes the verb and ni precedes each negated noun

evidence.notes: Taken from the rule's article behaviour and word order; the two-noun minimum is standard usage.

value: The reflexive pronoun stays between ne and the conjugated verb
In compound tenses ne and pas surround the auxiliary, with the reflexive pronoun before the auxiliary

evidence.notes: First entry from the given word order; the compound-tense placement is standard usage with medium confidence.

value: Only in the negative imperative; the affirmative imperative places the pronoun after the verb
The reflexive pronoun precedes the verb in the negative
No subject pronoun is expressed in the imperative

evidence.notes: Derived from the rule's formation and its contrast with the affirmative imperative.

value: Only in the negative imperative; in the affirmative the pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen
Object pronouns immediately precede the verb, after ne/n'
No subject pronoun is expressed in the imperative

evidence.notes: From the stated word order, the condition 'Only in negative imperative', and the trap about placement.

value: me, te, nous, vous come before le, la, les
le, la, les come before lui, leur
en always comes in second position, after the other object pronoun

evidence.notes: Derived from the rule's formation and the trap about third-person order; the position of en is standard usage.
